'''Annette Zippelius''' (born 25 June 1949) is a German [[physicist]], [[Leibniz Prize]] winner and an [[emeritus professor]] from the [[University of Göttingen]] known for her research on [[Complex fluid|complex fluids]] and [[soft matter]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Öffentlichkeitsarbeit |first=Georg-August-Universität Göttingen- |title=Zippelius, Annette, Prof. Dr. - Theoretical Physics (Uni-Phy) - Georg-August-University Göttingen |url=https://www.uni-goettingen.de/en/58063.html |access-date=2024-09-06 |website=Georg-August Universität Göttingen |language=de}}</ref> In 1988 she was appointed to the Chair of [[Theoretical physics|Theoretical Physics]] at the [[University of Göttingen]], making her the first woman to be appointed as a professor of C4 physics in Germany.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Öffentlichkeitsarbeit |first=Georg-August-Universität Göttingen- |title=About ITP - Georg-August-University Göttingen |url=https://www.uni-goettingen.de/en/about+itp/219706.html |access-date=2024-09-06 |website=Georg-August Universität Göttingen |language=de}}</ref> And in 1998, She was awarded the [[Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize]] for the construction of an exact network-model with the functioning proprieties of an associative memory.<ref name=":1" /> Most recently, in 2023 she was awarded the University Medal "In Publica Commoda" from the [[University of Göttingen]] for her service to the university.<ref name=":1" />

== Career ==
Annette Zippelius studied Physics at the [[University of Colorado]] in Boulder, USA. And in 1977, she finished her PhD at the [[Technical University of Munich]]. From 1978 to 1980, she was a postdoctoral associate at [[Harvard University]], and from 1980 to 1981 was a postdoctoral associate at [[Cornell University]].<ref name=":0" />

In 1983 she joined the [[Forschungszentrum Jülich]] as a researcher.<ref name=":0" />

She is currently an emeritus professor at the [[University of Göttingen]].<ref name=":0" />

== Awards and honors ==

* 1993: Member of the [[Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities]] (Akademie der Wissenschaften zu Göttingen).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://adw-goe.de/mitglieder/personendetails/person/annette-zippelius/|title=Prof. Dr. Annette Zippelius:&nbsp;Akademie der Wissenschaften zu Göttingen (AdW)|website=adw-goe.de|access-date=7 March 2019}}</ref>
* 1998: [[Leibniz Prize]] of the [[Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft]] (DFG)<ref name=":0" />
* 2002 – 2006: Member of the Executive Board of the [[German Physical Society]] ([[Deutsche Physikalische Gesellschaft]])<ref name=":0" />
* 2005 – 2011: Member of [https://www.wissenschaftsrat.de/nc/en/about.html The German Council of Science and Humanities] (Wissenschaftsrat)<ref name=":0" />
* 2007 – 2014: Max-Planck Fellow, [[Max Planck Institute for Dynamics and Self-Organization]], Göttingen<ref name=":0" />
* 2008: Elected Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]<ref name=":0" />
* 2022: [[Max Planck Medal]] of the [[German Physical Society]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dpg-physik.de/auszeichnungen/dpg-preise/max-planck-medaille/preistraeger|title=Max-Planck-Medal – Preisträgerinnen und Preisträger|publisher=[[German Physical Society]]|access-date=18 November 2021}}</ref>
* 2023: Awarded The University Medal "In Publica Commoda" from the [[University of Göttingen]]<ref name=":1" />
